hypothesis.statement: Treating MetaHuman Control Rig controls as SkeletalMesh morph targets can silently report successful lip sync while no production facial rig is actually driven.
hypothesis.action: Type every facial binding as MorphTarget or ControlRig, reject conflicting routes, route morphs only to the face mesh, and require a fail-closed AnimInstance interface that applies and reports actual Control Rig values.
hypothesis.expectedResult: Runtime presentation and the 57-sample QA runner use the same explicit target route and cannot confuse Control Rig controls with morph targets.

scopeBoundary: the C++ interface is a stable boundary; the future MetaHuman face Anim Blueprint must still implement it
the bridge does not assume undocumented direct UControlRig mutation APIs
successful curve transport still does not prove facial deformation quality
failureHandling: reject one curve registered as both morph and Control Rig
do not call SetMorphTarget for Control Rig routes
do not confirm viseme latency unless the target route was actually accepted
P36 runner rejects Control Rig evidence without a bridge-capable AnimInstance
P34 collector derives route from the DataAsset target enum and requires explicit bridge acknowledgement
decision: Keep production readiness false until a real MetaHuman face Anim Blueprint implements the bridge and P36 observes all required values.
